text:
maria: quick kickoff — we need to settle the API surface for fallback orchestration. do we let the router call a central "decision" service, or expose a policy DSL to runtimes and keep decisions local?
kevin: +1 to discussing. tradeoffs: central = single source of truth, easier canary metrics; local = lower latency and less cross-service blast radius.
jon: central gives us easier rollout experiments (A/B across segments) but is more stateful. how do we handle session affinity if central is down?
alexa: for oncall concern: central failure should degrade gracefully. prefer a model where runtimes have a small fallback policy that can run w/ stale rules if control plane is unreachable.
maria: idea: hybrid — central controller publishes signed, versioned policy bundles. runtimes evaluate locally with local telemetry + probes. controller handles global decisions, but runtime has permissive overrides.
kevin: sounds reasonable. need to define the bundle format + validation. also need TTL semantics for bundles and a quick escape hatch when bundle verification fails.
jon: sketch of a minimal bundle (proto/JSON):
```json
{
  "bundle_version": "2023-10-01T12:00:00Z",
  "policies": [
    { "id": "canary-route-1", "type": "percent", "percent": 5, "conditions": {"region": "us-east-1"} },
    { "id": "circuit-1", "type": "circuit", "error_threshold": 0.05, "window_s": 60 }
  ],
  "signature": "base64sig"
}
```
alexa: include an explicit "grace_mode": "allow" | "deny" | "safe-pass" so runtime knows what to do on staleness. and a "max_stale_s" field.
maria: good call. also need probe hooks: controller can request a runtime to run a lightweight probe against candidate variant and report pass/fail. probes should be idempotent and cheap.
kevin: we also need local heuristics for tail latency spikes: if latency > X ms for N requests, runtime should divert to fallback locally without consulting controller. that reduces happy-path latency during controller flapping.
jon: policy API should expose these knobs: local_fallback_thresholds, probe_policy, session_affinity_behavior, disable_remote_decisions (for private deployments).
maria: ops question — what's the telemetry contract? controller needs rolling aggregates but we should avoid full trace ingestion for every probe. maybe special probe metrics + percentiles + error counts per variant.
alexa: agree. a light telemetry envelope: {variant, probe_latency_p50/p95, error_rate, sample_rate}. send every 10s during canary period, backoff to 1m when stable.
kevin: and a health heartbeat for bundle freshness. if heartbeat stops for > max_stale_s, runtimes enter grace_mode.
deploy-bot: deploy job "publish-bundle v20231001" succeeded to edge 12 clusters — 5m ago.
maria: operational flow: 1) controller creates bundle, signs and increments version 2) controller streams version to picket services + edge registries 3) runtime validates signature + version, applies policy 4) runtime starts canary per policy and reports probe metrics 5) controller aggregates and either increases percent or rolls back
jon: fallback decision interface (runtime -> controller) should be async RPC with idempotency token, e.g., POST /decisions -> {request_id, snapshot_version, event}. controller may respond with instructions or 202 if processing.
kevin: also consider backpressure: if controller queues > threshold, runtimes should be documented to fall back locally. this prevents cascading when controller is overloaded.
alexa: SLO tie-in: define a per-tenant SLA that maps to policy aggressiveness. e.g., high-tier tenants get more conservative auto-fallback and more probes.
maria: long-term refactor: replace current ad-hoc handoff layer with a "policy gateway" lib we publish to runtimes. it should handle bundle validation, probe scheduling, local heuristics, and reporting. keep runtime-facing API tiny: checkFallback(variant, ctx) -> recommended_route.
kevin: proto example for checkFallback:
```proto
message CheckFallbackRequest {
  string request_id = 1;
  string bundle_version = 2;
  string variant = 3;
  map<string,string> context = 4;
}
message CheckFallbackResponse {
  enum Action { ROUTE=0; FALLBACK=1; PROBE=2 }
  Action action = 1;
  string reason = 2;
}
```
jon: neat. we should also define a diagnostics endpoint on runtimes so controller can fetch decision traces for debugging. keep traces sampled.
alexa: for incident playbooks: 1) detect spike in error_rate 2) controller triggers global quick-rollout to baseline 3) if controller unreachable, runtime local thresholds do auto-divert 4) page owners with bundle_version and sample traces
maria: next steps: - jon/kevin write a first pass bundle schema + proto - alexa draft telemetry envelope & playbook - i'll prototype the small policy gateway lib and post RFC draft next week
jon: will do + sync with infra about signing keys for bundles.
kevin: I'll prototype local heuristics and add unit tests for stale-bundle behavior.
alexa: I'll simulate controller outage in staging and validate grace_mode transitions.
maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup: keeping this thread as the canonical convo for the RFC follow-up.
